# Plan Result

## Epic

- Path: `epics/epic-01-approval-rules/`
- Goal: enforce the two finance approval rules inside `approveExpense`, so they hold for every caller and not only the router.
- Scope: self-approval is refused at any amount, and an expense of 50000 cents or more needs a manager. Rejection, expense editing and roles are out of scope.

## Stories

1. `story-01-01-enforce-approval-rules` runs in STRICT mode (permissions on a money path). It is a single walking-skeleton story, since `approveExpense` is the only place approval is decided. The checks go after the status check and before `store.update`, so a refusal changes nothing. `src/routes.js` stays untouched because it already turns thrown errors into a 400.

## First Story To Run

`story-01-01-enforce-approval-rules`

## Generated Files

- `epics/epic-01-approval-rules/index.md`
- `epics/epic-01-approval-rules/story-01-01-enforce-approval-rules/spec.md` (8 Given/When/Then criteria)
- `epics/epic-01-approval-rules/story-01-01-enforce-approval-rules/plan.md` (Decisions, test plan, traceability, `npm test`)
- `epics/epic-01-approval-rules/story-01-01-enforce-approval-rules/tasks.md`

I confirmed all four files exist. `ai-flow doctor` passes. It shows two warnings that were already there: the project docs are still templates, and the guard hook needs `ai-flow upgrade`. I did not touch application code.

## Assumptions

- "$500.00 or more" includes exactly $500.00, so the check is `amountCents >= 50000`.
- A manager who owns an expense can't approve it either. Rule 1 applies whatever the role.
- Self-approval is judged by the stored `expense.ownerId` against the looked-up actor, never against a field the caller supplies.
- Only `manager` counts as a manager role.

## Risks

- **Rule 2 can be bypassed through editing.** `PATCH /expenses` has no actor, ownership or role check. Anyone can lower the amount of a submitted $900 expense to $499 and then get it approved by a non-manager. This path doesn't reach the approval logic, so this plan doesn't cover it. Before the rules can really be called enforced, finance needs to decide who may edit an expense and whether its amount is frozen once it is submitted. I recommend a follow-up epic.
- `parseAmount` accepts negative amounts. A negative expense falls under the threshold and any role can approve it.
- `rejectExpense` has no role check, unlike `approveExpense`. The agreed rules don't cover it, so I only flagged it.

## Clarification Readiness

Ready. The only real ambiguity was whether the $500 threshold is inclusive, and the wording settles it. The edit-path decision above is a separate scope question, not a blocker for this story.

## Recommended Next Command

Run `/flow-run` on `epics/epic-01-approval-rules/story-01-01-enforce-approval-rules` in STRICT mode. I'd also ask finance about the edit-path decision now, so the follow-up epic isn't left waiting.
